So I fail to understand the source and the cause of your concern on this specific matter. I may understand other things, I may be on your page, on your side, on other things, but I don't understand your concern here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution does not know what the Chamber have or does not have. We have referred to some instances in our motion, and I cited some other instances just now. The Prosecution's position is that anything that the Trial Chamber looks at to inform themselves about the case, the parties have the right to receive and should be informed of. If that is publicly available books, that is hearsay evidence, I assume, that has some relevance, but the Trial Chamber needs to inform the parties. So I believe that is a basic fair trial issue that is being raised now. I don't quite -- I think we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, each -- I don't know what each and every Judge does, of course, but I can assure you, Mr. Marcussen, that the Trial Chamber, as a whole, will only look at the evidence on record, and I think that's only natural, the most normal thing you [as interpreted] can do. We can't look at anything else. I mean, the Trial Chamber, as such, as a whole. I mean, I think you may have ideas that -- I mean, if, individually, you may have ideas. It's not at all relevant. The Trial Chamber only analyses the evidence on record. You know very well that I, personally, made a stance in court on many occasions. I don't understand your concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me add to this, yes. If there is something of relevance to the case, if the Trial Chamber has any intention, proprio motu, which is not the case yet, then, of course, it would seek the views of both parties, should an important piece of evidence be admitted. But right now we've got nothing that we're hiding. So that's how things are right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have made my position clear, and there is a distinction between material that's been consulted and material that ultimately is admitted into evidence. I, of course, appreciate that fact. Again, we submit that all material that the Trial Chamber or the individual Judges consults, in the view of informing itself about the case or with a view to find out whether or not there are things out there which they think should be admitted into evidence, the parties should know about. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, does this -- is this tantamount to saying -- sometimes it's difficult to understand you, but does this mean, for instance, that -- it was said by Mr. Seselj that Wikileaks had been sort of been taken on by the Serbian press, and mention was made of documents coming from the Dutch Embassy that may be related to the Seselj case. Does this mean that in the ICTY press review -- I've read that article, I must tell you that I've read it - is that what you mean to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I don't believe, Your Honours, that the Wikileaks issue have any relevance to the merits of this case, so obviously that is a completely different matter. But if the Trial Chamber is looking at -- to inform itself about issues related to the case within the time-frame, within the geographical scope of the case, with a view to better understand who players are, what actually happened, anything like that, the parties should be appraised of. And the Prosecution have simply asked that any such material be disclosed to the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please move on, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think we should move on. But, Mr. Marcussen, just one small example. Mr. Seselj's state of health. He spoke of arrhythmia, of heart problems. So there are two possibilities. Am I not entitled to seek some information as to his complaints by reading scientific literature on the topic? Or if I were to read the definition given to "arrhythmia," do I have to tell you that I read something about arrhythmia? Do you seek to control what a Judge does?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I don't think the current state of health of the accused has anything to do with the charges against him in this case, so I don't -- I don't -- my answer to your question about the medical issues would be, No. We're not seeking to control what the Judges do. We are seeking disclosure of information that the Judges look at that's relevant to the case, and not other issues. I don't know how else I can explain it. I ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You have made your point clear, Mr. Marcussen. Let's move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is another important pending motion. Again, I understand that a decision is imminent. It is the decision on the Prosecution's motion from 20th of July this year, where we seek to add additional witnesses to our witness lists to testify or to provide evidence about tendered statements and admitted statements into evidence. We believe that we have the right to present our case in full. Our fair trial rights require that we're allowed to call these witnesses. And as I mentioned earlier, once we get the decision, we will obviously look at it. It may raise some appellate issue, but there's another issue, which is that the Prosecution has, as you know, refrained from contacting any of these witnesses -- potential witnesses about their knowledge of the allegations made by the particular witnesses. We have done that in order not to be seen to in any way interfere with the investigation that Your Honours ordered on the 29th of June, 2010. But what I want to alert the Trial Chamber to is that it means that if the motion is granted, the Prosecution will have to go and determine whether or not there are people who have knowledge of these events that can be called. So if the motion is granted, we would need some time to do that. That is not an attempt to obstruct or delay things. It is simply a necessity for us to be able to present the evidence. The final thing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, earlier on I was saying that we were at a stage of the 98 bis proceedings, and now you are speaking about witnesses that you plan to call. I remind you that you have rested your case. A decision has been issued that as of the 1st of June you were not allowed to seek to adduce new evidence, and I think you've totally forgotten about it. I'm wondering whether you are not sort of linking this up to the fact that the 98 bis proceedings are just about to be held, and you don't want them. You mentioned a pending motion. You are going to have a decision. I told you that all the decisions would be issued before the winter recess. They'll be none left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to say that we have still some major motions to adjudicate, so I'm not quite sure -- I can't say that everything is done now, that everything's finished. We'll see. I mean, that's my personal opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection or a remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mr. Seselj. You will have time to answer. But let Mr. Marcussen finish, because he's now tackling a very important matter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He interrupts me. I'm also speaking about important things. When he interrupts me, you immediately allow him to speak. I always speak about more important things than Mr. Marcussen does. What he has been saying now has nothing to do with anything of importance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, we're now doing extra time. I just wanted to remind you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I have a clarification to ask. Is it the Chamber's view or is it the President's view that the Prosecution has requested to call additional witnesses because we want to delay the 98 bis hearing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That is not a decision of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a personal opinion, my very clear personal opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, that's certainly not the case. The motion was filed as soon as these issues arose -- was filed as soon as these issues arose. They came up with the last court witnesses that testified, and actually the motion -- initial motion was made within the dead-line set by the Trial Chamber of the 1st of June this year. So not only was the motion filed on time, it was filed as soon as the issues arose. We supplemented the motion as soon as the last witness had testified, where these issues also arise. So I take strong issue with the characterisation of this as being some delaying tactic. It's completely proper filings we have filed. We have not closed our case. It may be that the Trial Chamber thinks that the Prosecution case is over. The Prosecution has not closed its case. The Prosecution has made clear all the time that it cannot close its case until these evidentiary matters have been settled. Now, a few issues came up today with respect to VS-026. The Prosecution would request disclosure of the medical reports that the Trial Chamber have received so we can understand the Trial Chamber's oral decision about his ability to testify. I would also note that the Prosecution also tendered VS-026's testimony in the Milosevic case on the days of 3rd, 4th, and 10th June, 2003. I might have overlooked it, but I don't think there was a decision on that. But it's still our position that we think that testimony should be part of the evidence in the case. The final thing I'd like to raise is the issue of -- maybe, actually, we need to go into private session for this, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before you take the floor, Mr. Seselj, in open session: As far as the appointment of the amicus curiae, confidential and ex parte, the Trial Chamber has decided to lift the ex parte portion of this document. So you will be provided with the Registrar's document and information about the amicus curiae. Mr. Seselj, this is what I wanted to share with you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will tell you very quickly what I have to say. First of all, let me inform you that I handed over to the secretary of the Chamber this document, this letter of Jovica Jovanovic, to my lawyer, Milan Terzic. So they are going to distribute that to you. Photocopies have been made for the members of the Trial Chamber and for the OTP. I want the transcript to reflect that. Secondly, at the outset the Prosecutor said that the trial cannot go on without a medical report. That is simply not true. I insisted here several times that the state of my health has nothing to do with the proceedings. Even today, I was more than capable of taking part in the proceedings, and you saw that for yourselves. They say that my life is not threatened. If somebody were to examine Mr. Marcussen now, perhaps you would find out that he is in a far more difficult situation than I am. If you just look at his face, the redness of his face, I am concerned about his health. But there's lots of them on the OTP --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, don't be witty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not going to go into that anymore. I am going to allow you to finish this administrative proceeding, and I will just say something about what Mr. Marcussen said. Mr. Marcussen said that the Prosecution is asking for more witnesses to be added. I do not remember receiving this motion. If I do not remember receiving it, that means that I never received it. If I did receive some motion to that effect, the names of these new witnesses had not been mentioned. I oppose that sharply. The Prosecution has had all of eight years to find witnesses, to instruct them, to prepare them, to lead them and so on. Now, eight years later, for them to be looking for new witnesses, this is a new scandal. In 2003, if they did not have witnesses to support their indictment that would lead to a finding of guilty, it is way too late now. You saw that in 2003, they had nothing. They were walking around like geese in a fog. The indictment was issued without them having anything. Judge O-gon Kwon confirmed the indictment just off the cuff, and then they tried to find witnesses in this and that and every other way, and this has been tellingly demonstrated here in the courtroom. And now they want new witnesses. Well, these new witnesses can only be OTP officials. Or they should take Tomislav Nikolic and Aleksandar Vukovic. They would be prepared to testify to anything now. When they were prepared to plant this kind of lie, that I was preparing somebody's assassination, they will not stop at anything. One of them was my deputy and the other one was my secretary-general. Ideal witnesses. They will say anything you want them to say. However, I think these things have to be brought to a halt. Why would I cross-examine these new witnesses? Why would I bother with these new witnesses? I am not going to bother with them at all. What do you mean, new witnesses eight years later? Eight years means almost 20 years after the war developments that the indictment pertains to. And now they have found new witnesses. I do not believe that. I really think that they are inventing this. I'm convinced that they do not have any new witnesses at all. Again, they are reaching out for this and that and the other thing, like geese in the fog, as I said, because after a 98 bis hearing, nothing else could follow but an acquittal. The Prosecution knows that even if you wanted to make every effort to find me guilty, you have no grounds for doing that, and that is their nightmare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Maybe the accused has finished, but I think all -- everything he has said has been based on a misunderstanding. There is no new motion that has been filed. It's a 1st June motion that you were given in August; I think it was on the 13th of August. So -- and I believe you addressed the same motion at the last admin hearing. So, yeah, I hope that could take care of it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not received a list of new witnesses. Now, whether that exists in that motion, that's what Mr. Marcussen has to say to you. Did you include that in that motion of yours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, a motion was filed; that is true. The Prosecution wishes to add two witnesses to its 65 ter list. And as you receive or get acknowledgments of receipt, I believe you signed these two acknowledgments of the receipt, one on the 8th of July and the other on the 16th of August, and you have not responded. You have been informed of these motions. Maybe this has escaped you, since we are dealing with a great number of documents. The Prosecutor is seeking leave to hear two witnesses, and the Trial Chamber is about to rule on this. You haven't -- you didn't respond, and you respond belatedly to say that you don't wish to hear these witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that Mano Milovanovic? Sorry, I do not know these names. Are these protected witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into closed session. The Prosecutor will give you the two names.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that he doesn't know their names either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, if the name has been mentioned in public, an order needs to be issued with a view to redact this name. All you need to do, Mr. Seselj, is to look at the first and last name. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have that. It's not unknown to me. I thought that these were actually new witnesses, new real witnesses. The fact that the OTP is going to hear itself is something that is going to bring great joy to me here, fun and games. It so turned out that they do not have a single witness for any one of my crimes. Perhaps I've committed a great many crimes, but they don't have a single witness. So now they are going to bring themselves in as witnesses. Fun and games. However, please bear in mind that you have to do that in public session when you are hearing the prosecutors as witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will issue a decision on this matter. Whatever the case may be, I have stated that we had planned to hold a hearing on the 18th and 19th of January. One will be an administrative hearing. We will meet then, because we shall have the winter recess in the meantime. We shall meet again mid-January for an administrative hearing, and I hope that by that time all the decisions will have been handed down. Things will be much clearer then. And by the 19th of January we might then have the expert report. I apologise to the interpreters, who thought they may finish at 5.30. I apologise for this, and I wish all and everyone a very pleasant evening.
